# zyxel Provider

The Zyxel provider manages router configuration directly through the router's
encrypted `DAL` HTTP API. It needs no CLI, Python, or agent at runtime.

> **Status: experimental.** Read paths and mock-router lifecycle tests pass, and
> a read-only plan has been verified against a physical router. Live writes have
> not been verified on hardware. Review every plan and keep a router backup.

## Requirements

- Terraform 1.14 or newer
- Go 1.27 or newer, only when building the provider from source

## Installation

The provider is published on the
[Terraform Registry](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/VincentSchmid/zyxel/latest).
Declare it in your configuration:

```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    zyxel = {
      source  = "VincentSchmid/zyxel"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}
```

```sh
terraform init
```

Terraform downloads the published binary; no Go toolchain or local build is needed.
Remove any existing `dev_overrides` entry for this provider to use the published
version. For local development, see the
[development instructions](https://github.com/VincentSchmid/terraform-provider-zyxel#development).

## Example Usage

```hcl
provider "zyxel" {}

data "zyxel_status" "router" {}

resource "zyxel_nat_rule" "https" {
  name                = "HTTPS"
  protocol            = "tcp"
  external_port_start = 443
  external_port_end   = 443
  internal_client     = "192.168.1.240"
  internal_port_start = 443
  internal_port_end   = 443
}

resource "zyxel_dhcp_reservation" "nas" {
  mac_address  = "02:00:00:00:00:20"
  ipv4_address = "192.168.1.20"
}

# Allow only Cloudflare to reach the HTTPS host, then drop everyone else.
data "zyxel_cloudflare_ipv4_ranges" "https" {}

resource "zyxel_acl_rule" "cloudflare" {
  for_each = toset(data.zyxel_cloudflare_ipv4_ranges.https.ranges)

  name                   = "Cloudflare-${replace(each.value, "/", "-")}"
  action                 = "accept"
  order                  = index(data.zyxel_cloudflare_ipv4_ranges.https.ranges, each.value) + 1
  source_cidr            = each.value
  destination_cidr       = "192.168.1.240/32"
  destination_port_start = 443
  destination_port_end   = 443
}
```

## Credentials

Set the complete pair through provider configuration or through both
`ZYXEL_USER` and `ZYXEL_PASS`; the provider never mixes a configured value with
an environment value. `ZYXEL_HOST` supplies the host. The provider does not read
`.env` files or credentials from disk.

The router firmware limits concurrent administrator logins. Operations sharing
one provider client are serialized, but avoid running several Terraform
processes against the router at the same time.

## Firewall Services

Use `zyxel_service` to manage reusable TCP, UDP, ICMP, ICMPv6, or other IP
protocol objects and reference them with `zyxel_acl_rule.service_id`. Both
services and inline ACLs accept compact `source_ports` and `destination_ports`
selectors such as `"*"`, `"443"`, and `"443-445"`.

Service deletion is refused while any ACL references it, to prevent the router
from cascading deletion to associated rules. See the service resource docs for
replacement safety and examples.

## Schema

### Optional

- `host` (String) Router hostname, IP address, or `http(s)://` URL. Defaults to `ZYXEL_HOST` and uses HTTP when no scheme is given.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Router administrator password. May be set with `ZYXEL_PASS`; provider configuration takes precedence.
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) HTTP timeout in seconds for each router request. Defaults to 10 seconds.
- `username` (String, Sensitive) Router administrator username. May be set with `ZYXEL_USER`; provider configuration takes precedence.
